text:
The text contrasts two perspectives on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme of inherent evil, suggesting that humans are naturally savage and descend into barbarism when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy posits that humans are naturally good and free, and it is society that corrupts them. The similarity in presentation lies in both texts addressing the fundamental nature of humanity and the role of environment or society in shaping behavior, but they differ sharply in their conclusions: Golding argues for innate depravity, while Rousseau argues for innate goodness corrupted by external forces.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
